name: Fujifilm Neopan 1600 Professional
notes: Fujifilm Data Sheet 'NEOPAN 1600 Professional' (Neopan 1600 Super Presto), 4 pages, scanned black-and-white drawings (bilevel, with broken grid lines). Document AF3-608E; date taken from the print code EIGI-99.1 next to the reference number on page 4 (no other date printed). Speed EI 1600/33 deg.

curves: page 4, section 10, four plots (SPD [Super Prodol], D-76, Fujidol E, Microfine; all 20 C small tank), each with three development times. x axis is log H in lux-seconds as printed (-4.0 to 1.0), y is density. The sheet does not say the exposure light or the density measurement. Printed average gradients (G-bar) per curve: SPD 6 1/4 min 0.90, 4 1/4 min 0.77, 2 3/4 min 0.58; D-76 7 1/2 min 0.81, 5 1/4 min 0.59, 4 min 0.48; Fujidol E 6 1/2 min 0.76, 5 min 0.62, 4 1/2 min 0.54; Microfine 8 min 0.70, 6 1/2 min 0.60, 5 1/2 min 0.52.

v is SPD 4 1/4 min: page 2 lists SPD [Super Prodol] first, EI 1600 at 20 C = 4 1/4 min, and the automatic processor examples on page 3 use SPD too; the other SPD times are v-spd-6.25 and v-spd-2.75 (plot 'curves'). A plot name can be used once per sheet, so the other developers are stored as extra plots 'curves-d76' (v-d76-7.5, -5.25, -4), 'curves-fujidol-e' (v-fujidol-e-6.5, -5, -4.5) and 'curves-microfine' (v-microfine-8, -6.5, -5.5); build.py reads only 'curves'. By the sheet's tables (20 C): D-76 7 1/2 min and Fujidol E 6 1/2 min are the EI 1600 times, Microfine 8 min is the EI 800 time (Microfine EI 1600 is not listed), so the Microfine set is not an EI 1600 development.

Curves start at log H about -3.8 (D-min plateau 0.19-0.20 for SPD, 0.19 D-76 and Fujidol E, 0.17 Microfine) and stop at log H about 0.2-0.25, where each leads into its G-bar label (labels masked). Where two or three curves of one plot lie on top of each other (toe below log H about -2.9, and Microfine 6 1/2 vs 5 1/2 min around log H -2.2 to -1.9) the traced lines are good to about 0.02 D; the hints in those places were taken from the ink edges.

sensitivity: page 3, section 9, 'Spectrogram to Daylight (5400K)', a plotted curve (not a photograph). Axis is 'Relative Sensitivity (log)' with no numbers, only an arrow marking 1.0 log unit between two grid lines; y here is relative, taking the lower grid line as 0.0 and the upper as 1.0 (zero point arbitrary). The curve runs from about 389 nm to about 648 nm and ends in a steep drop from about 640 nm, so the last 5 nm samples are approximate.
Grain: no granularity (RMS) or print grain value is printed in this sheet; no resolving power either. Section 11 has time vs G-bar curves (not traced).
